name: MKOBJ
desc: Covers MKOBJ property-pair arrays and ordered overrides, omitted lists via null, ignored null entries, later-key precedence, computed string names, functional construction, arbitrary own properties, independent values, namespaces, dates and SPLIT metadata, validation, error propagation, and resource limits. Invalid argument counts are INVALID_GRAFT; invalid runtime names and shapes are INVALID_TARGET.

tests.name: Overrides without an initial property list
tests.desc: A null initial list is followed by name/value pairs. Values may have any JSON type, and both names and values evaluate in the caller scope without name coercion.

tests.name: Property-pair arrays
tests.desc: Exactly one array-valued operand holds two-element arrays. Both empty and populated lists are supported. Pair positions are strict and names remain strings.

tests.name: Input list is borrowed only for evaluation
Pair list constructor evaluates names and values
Nested CONCAT assembles a property list
Null entries and ordered overrides
tests.desc: Null omits the initial list or a whole list entry, never a name or property value. Overrides are appended in argument order; malformed entries and failing expressions are not hidden by later overwrites.

tests.name: Computed null initial list constructs an empty object
Null entries do not remove an earlier property
Null entries before between and after pairs
Empty list can be followed by overrides
Overrides append new properties and replace list properties
Repeated overrides keep their last value
Null override value remains a present property
List duplicates then overrides follow one order
Computed override names and values use the original caller
Null property name is not an ignored entry
Malformed earlier pair is not hidden by an override
Overwritten value expressions are still evaluated
Overwritten list value expressions are still evaluated
Invalid initial list is not ignored when overrides follow
Former alternating form requires a null initial list
Former parallel arrays are invalid argument counts
Invalid arity is not trapped by ANY
Invalid override arity is not trapped by NONE
Functional property construction
tests.desc: MAP, FILTER, REDUCE, and PROPS produce or transform pair arrays. Null MAP results omit properties, while duplicate computed names follow input order.

tests.name: MAP constructs computed properties and omits null results
MAP collisions keep the later input value
FILTER over PROPS removes underscore-prefixed names
MAP over PROPS preserves names and changes values
MAP over PROPS computes new names and omits selected properties
Renaming collisions follow sorted PROPS order
REDUCE can assemble the complete property list
Parallel source arrays can be paired with MAP
Names and duplicate-key precedence
tests.desc: Names are exact strings with no normalization or coercion. Empty, numeric-looking, Unicode, control, and host-special names become own properties. Repeated names keep the last value in list or override order.

tests.name: Invalid names and shapes
tests.desc: Names must be strings and non-null entries must be two-element arrays. Runtime shape and name failures are INVALID_TARGET. Missing initial arguments and incomplete overrides are INVALID_GRAFT, including inside match probes.

tests.name: Flat list is not a list of pairs
Scopes, independence, and value semantics
tests.desc: Names and values use the original caller current node. CONST, STASH, TEMP, common expressions, and matching contexts retain their ordinary value semantics. Result edits cannot modify referenced source data.

tests.name: IS compares a complete constructed object
Parsed dates retain virtual fields in stash
Pending deletion in values is invalid
Subsequent COPY pairs can read the result
Computed key does not rebind the value current node
Failure propagation and limits
tests.desc: Missing values, invalid nested expressions, and explicit FAIL propagate without publishing a partially constructed object. Match probes trap INVALID_TARGET while RESOURCE_LIMIT and unsupported-host failures remain fatal.
